topics.title: Inequalities and Regions
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: identify and use inequality symbols. (k s)
illustrate inequalities on the number lines. (u s)
solve linear inequalities in one unknown. (u s)
represent linear inequalities graphically. (k u s)
form simple linear inequalities for regions on a graph. (u s)

body.text: A commuter taxi in Kampala is meant to carry no more than 14 passengers. A bag of cement must weigh at least 50 kg. Neither statement gives one exact number. Each describes a range of allowed numbers. An inequality is a statement that one quantity is bigger or smaller than another.

items: ≤ means 'is less than or equal to'.
≥ means 'is greater than or equal to'.

body.text: The open end of the symbol always faces the bigger number. If p is the number of passengers in the taxi, then p ≤ 14. If m is the mass of a bag of cement in kilograms, then m ≥ 50.

Draw a number line and mark the boundary number with a circle. Use an open, empty circle for < or >, because the boundary number is not included. Use a filled circle for ≤ or ≥, because the boundary number is included. Then draw an arrow along the line in the direction of the allowed numbers.
For x > 2, draw an open circle at 2 and an arrow to the right. For −1 ≤ x < 4, draw a filled circle at −1, an open circle at 4, and a line joining them.

We solve an inequality in almost the same way as an equation. We may add or subtract the same number on both sides. We may multiply or divide both sides by the same positive number. There is one extra rule: when we multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, we must reverse the inequality sign.

body.title: Solve 2x + 7 < x + 10
steps: Subtract x from both sides: x + 7 < 10.
Subtract 7 from both sides: x < 3.
On a number line: an open circle at 3 and an arrow to the left.
Check with x = 2: 2 × 2 + 7 = 11 and 2 + 10 = 12. 11 < 12 is true.

body.title: Solve 5 − 3x ≥ 11, where the sign turns round
steps: Subtract 5 from both sides: −3x ≥ 6.
Divide both sides by −3. Dividing by a negative number reverses the sign: x ≤ −2.

body.title: Solve a double inequality and list the integers
steps: Solve −1 < 2x + 3 ≤ 9.
Subtract 3 from all three parts: −4 < 2x ≤ 6.
Divide all three parts by 2: −2 < x ≤ 3.
The integers that satisfy this are −1, 0, 1, 2 and 3. Note that −2 is not included, but 3 is.

body.title: Form and solve an inequality from a story
steps: Okello has UGX 20,000. He buys a mathematical set for UGX 6,500 and some pens at UGX 1,500 each. How many pens can he buy?
Let n be the number of pens. The total cost must not be more than his money.
Subtract 6,500 from both sides: 1,500n ≤ 13,500.
Divide both sides by 1,500: n ≤ 9.
Okello can buy at most 9 pens.

body.text: An inequality in x and y describes a region of the Cartesian plane. A region is an area of the graph. First draw the boundary line by replacing the inequality sign with =. Draw a solid line for ≤ or ≥, because points on the line are included. Draw a broken (dashed) line for < or >, because points on the line are not included.

Next, decide which side of the line is wanted. Choose a test point that is not on the line, often (0, 0). If the test point makes the inequality true, its side is wanted. Many Ugandan textbooks shade the unwanted region, so that the wanted region stays clear. Always say which way you have shaded.
For y < 2x + 1, draw the line y = 2x + 1 as a broken line. Test (0, 0): 0 < 2 × 0 + 1 gives 0 < 1, which is true. So the side containing the origin is the wanted region.

body.title: Find the inequalities for a triangular region
steps: A region is a triangle with corners at (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 4). Its edges are included.
The left edge lies on the y-axis, the line x = 0. The region is to its right, so x ≥ 0.
The bottom edge lies on the x-axis, the line y = 0. The region is above it, so y ≥ 0.
The sloping edge joins (4, 0) and (0, 4). Each point on it has x + y = 4.
Test a point inside, such as (1, 1): 1 + 1 = 2, which is less than 4. So x + y ≤ 4.
The region is described by x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and x + y ≤ 4.

body.title: Foxes and chickens
body.text: Draw a large coordinate grid on the floor with chalk, or on a sheet of paper. One group places bottle tops as chickens at chosen points. The other group builds fences to protect them. Each fence is a straight line given as an inequality, such as x ≥ 1 or y < 5. The chickens must all lie inside the fenced region. Swap roles and try to use as few fences as possible.
Start with 2 < 5, which is true. Multiply both sides by −1. Is −2 < −5 still true? Mark both numbers on a number line. Why does multiplying by a negative number turn the inequality sign round?

Use an open circle for < and >, and a filled circle for ≤ and ≥. Solve inequalities like equations, but reverse the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative number. On a graph, draw a solid boundary for ≤ or ≥ and a broken one for < or >, and use a test point to find the wanted region.
